author: chatgpt-codex-connector
body:
Align ProductTeamModel read filter with stored team_id values
The new product scoping filter always rewrites queries to the effective (parent) team ID, but writes are still free to store the original child team ID. In paths like visual_review where code still passes the request team ID directly on create/update, child-team data becomes unreadable because reads end up with contradictory predicates (team_id=parent from manager scoping plus explicit team_id=child filters). This will surface as missing repos/runs for environment teams with parent_team_id set unless team IDs are normalized on write (or reads stop rewriting).
Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

author: chatgpt-codex-connector
body:
Preserve backward compatibility for queued diff tasks
This signature change makes team_id mandatory for the Celery task, which breaks any messages already queued with the previous one-arg payload during rolling deploys or retry/requeue windows. For those jobs, @with_team_scope() will interpret the old run_id string as team_id and raise TypeError before task logic runs, leaving runs stuck in processing. The task should accept the legacy shape (e.g., optional team_id and fallback lookup from run_id) until old messages are drained.
Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

author: haacked
body:
blocking: This pattern list catches read-shaped methods but misses the highest-blast-radius operations: Model.objects.update(...), Model.objects.delete(), Model.objects.create(...), Model.objects.bulk_create(...), plus the async variants (aget, aupdate, acount, aexists, aiterator). Model.objects.filter(...).delete() is incidentally covered (the filter pattern matches), but a top-level Model.objects.delete() is not, and update mass-mutates other tenants if the scope is missing.
Add at minimum the mutating verbs and async variants to the pattern-either list:
- pattern: $MODEL.objects.update(...)
- pattern: $MODEL.objects.delete()
- pattern: $MODEL.objects.create(...)
- pattern: $MODEL.objects.bulk_create(...)

- pattern: $MODEL.objects.values(...)

author: haacked
body:
blocking: A subclass that overrides initial (or finalize_response) without calling super() silently runs without the URL-team-id context, so middleware-set current_team_id wins and the token is never reset. The existing __init_subclass__ protected-methods check above does not cover these, so the failure is silent at class-definition time. The blast radius is small today (only the four visual_review models on ProductTeamModel), but this becomes a tripwire as more models migrate.
Add both names to the protected list, or move the context setup into dispatch() where overrides are uncommon. Cheapest fix:
"initial": "Team-scope context is set here. Override safe_get_team_id() instead.",
"finalize_response": "Team-scope context is reset here. Do not override.",

author: haacked
body:
blocking: With bind=True, an upgraded worker pulling an old payload [run_id_str] from the broker calls wrapper(self, run_id_str). The decorator indexes args[1] for team_id, gets the run_id string, fails isinstance(team_id, int), and raises TypeError. autoretry_for does not include TypeError, so the message dies at max_retries=3 and the Run row stays in processing indefinitely.
Two options, in order of operational simplicity:

Document a queue-drain step in the deploy runbook for this PR. Visual_review's footprint is small enough that this is probably enough.
Ship a transition shim that accepts either signature, deploy, drain naturally, remove the shim in a follow-up:

@shared_task(bind=True, ...)
def process_run_diffs(self, *args) -> None:
    if len(args) == 1:
        run_id = args[0]
        from products.visual_review.backend.facade import api
        team_id = api.get_run(UUID(run_id)).team_id
    elif len(args) == 2:
        team_id, run_id = args
    else:
        raise TypeError(f"process_run_diffs: unexpected args {args!r}")
    with team_scope(team_id):
        _process_run_diffs_inner(self, team_id, run_id)
Codex bot raised this too.

author: haacked
body:
suggestion: This and _resolve_effective_team_id in product_mixin.py:40 are the same algorithm with the same 4-line cache-invariant comment. The product_mixin docstring even says "This prevents the two approaches from drifting", but the structural fix for drift is one helper, not a comment. Once 35+ models adopt this, any change to the cache-invalidation rules has to land in two places, and a future contributor will fix one and miss the other.
Extract to one private helper (e.g. posthog.models.scoping._team_resolver.resolve_effective_team_id) and call from both sites. The persons-DB vs. product-DB distinction is only about how the result is applied (subquery+JOIN vs. plain filter), not how it's computed.

author: haacked
body:
suggestion: Repo.objects.unscoped() (the queryset method) and Repo.unscoped (this Manager attribute) are two different surfaces with the same name. Tests use the queryset method everywhere; the README points admin at the Manager attribute. A future contributor who autocompletes Repo.unscoped.filter(...) thinking they're being explicit about scoping gets every team's rows back.
Two options:

Drop this attribute and standardize on Repo.objects.unscoped(). Update the admin guidance in posthog/models/scoping/README.md to match.
Rename the attribute so the two surfaces aren't the same word, e.g. all_teams = models.Manager().

If the attribute stays, the comment should at least name the failure mode rather than the linter rule:
  
    
      
        Suggested change
      
    
    
      
          
            
                unscoped = models.Manager()  # noqa: DJ012 — both are managers, ruff misclassifies this
          
          
            
                # Escape hatch for admin / migrations / contexts that need a manager
          
          
            
                # bypassing fail-closed scoping. Order matters: `objects` must be declared
          
          
            
                # first so Django picks ProductTeamManager as `_default_manager`. Reach for
          
          
            
                # this only when the queryset method `Model.objects.unscoped()` doesn't
          
          
            
                # work (rare; admin and raw-SQL migrations are the main legitimate uses).
          
          
            
                unscoped = models.Manager()  # noqa: DJ012

author: haacked
body:
nit: self.team is @cached_property, so "team" in self.__dict__ correctly detects the cached case. That contract is implicit though: if anyone ever switches self.team to plain @property (or a method), this check silently becomes False forever, parent_team_id becomes always-None, and every read falls through to the subquery+JOIN path with no test failure to flag it.
Two ways to make it less brittle:

A one-line comment above this line: # Requires self.team to be @cached_property (line 297). Plain @property breaks the optimization silently.
Or reach for the cache directly: parent_team_id = self.__dict__.get("team", None) and self.team.parent_team_id. Same behavior, but the dependency is on the dict key, not the descriptor type.

Either way, easier to spot if self.team is ever changed.

author: haacked
body:
suggestion: team_scope, for_team, and with_team_scope trust the caller to pass canonical team_id. A caller who writes with team_scope(child_team_id): gets zero rows from any read. Data lives at the parent, the filter is on the child. No error, no log.
Have these three call resolve_effective_team_id themselves. One Team lookup at scope entry; the framework guarantees correctness regardless of caller hygiene. Matches the cost the old read-time resolution paid, amortized over the scope.
If the per-scope lookup is too much, add an explicit canonical: bool = False kwarg so misuse is an argument error instead of zero rows.
